intent: Determine whether substring-presence-only detection (flag any outbound occurrence of a fetched private value) is sufficient to catch purpose-bound leaks. Hypothesis: presence alone is enough.
riskRationale: A design negative result. Cheap to run; its value is preventing a wrong, weaker gate design from being built and trusted.

constraints.detail: DISPROVED. The benign in-purpose use and the leak contain byte-identical occurrences of the same email. Under presence-only logic both are flagged (or neither is); the two cases are indistinguishable without comparing declared purpose to sink purpose.

Re-running the suite with the purpose-mismatch branch disabled (presence-only behavior) turns the benign-vs-leak separation off: the planted-leak test goes RED. Only PURPOSE_COMPATIBILITY restores correct separation.

observations.detail: email fetched for send_calendar_invite, placed INTO the send_calendar_invite tool call. Value present in outbound.
same email present in a general_summary user_message. Value present in outbound — identical presence signal to the benign case.

actions.detail: Both cases satisfy 'value appears in an outbound sink'. The ONLY differing field is sink.purpose (send_calendar_invite vs general_summary).
Disabled the purpose-mismatch branch in gate.ts (reduces gate to presence-only)
actions.result: north-star planted-leak test fails (verdict 'pass' instead of 'leak') — presence-only cannot catch the leak without also flagging the benign use

assertions.detail: benign and leak share identical value-presence; differ only by purpose
bound-purpose vs sink-purpose comparison is the sole separating signal

evidence.note: Recorded so the weaker design is not re-attempted.
Disabling the `allowed.includes(sink.purpose)` branch reproduces presence-only behavior and turns the planted-leak tests RED; restoring returns 16/16 GREEN.
PURPOSE_COMPATIBILITY is the encoded fix for the disproved hypothesis.

mechanisms: Prevents building a presence-only redactor that would either miss leaks or destroy benign in-purpose use.
Justifies the load-bearing role of PURPOSE_COMPATIBILITY in policy.ts for any downstream consumer of the gate.
projection.notes: Context only. Not a score. A verified-disproved result is a first-class artifact per MY_REPO_SHAPE.
